meta.source_system: HTTP/2 stream state machine (one stream as seen by one endpoint), transcribed from RFC 9113 section 5.1 Figure 2 and the per-state bullet lists. RFC 9113 is a public standard (Internet Standards Track technical specification; obsoletes RFC 7540).
meta.source_citation: RFC 9113 (June 2022), section 5.1 'Stream States', Figure 2 + per-state bullet lists + the END_STREAM separate-event paragraph. Per-edge citations in meta.edges_with_citations.
meta.semantics_class: event: the actions are protocol frame events (with the figure's own PP/H/ES/R abbreviations); their names are part of the behavior and do not follow state renamings -- candidate groups in groups/ declare semantics "fixed". The relabel rows in expected.json are the diagnostic contrast reading, not the protocol-true one.
meta.encoding: states 7..15 = unreachable padding (self-loop only); undeclared (state, event) pairs self-loop with reward 0
meta.reward_rule: rewards all zero: the stream-state layer defines no payoff; the reward layer carries no information, all conclusions come from the transition layer

transcription_notes: NOT COLLECTED  idle -> closed via a higher-valued intervening stream identifier: sec.5.1 'idle' bullet says 'Opening a stream with a higher-valued stream identifier causes the stream to transition immediately to a closed state; note that this transition is not shown in the diagram.' The RFC itself omits it from Figure 2; not transcribed (same policy as the tcp case's treatment of the any-state RST note).

KEPT via the separate-event rule: 'For the purpose of state transitions, the END_STREAM flag is processed as a separate event to the frame that bears it; a HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM flag set can cause two state transitions.' (sec.5.1, right after Figure 2). Hence 'send ES' / 'recv ES' are standalone events and a HEADERS frame with ES chains two edges (e.g. idle --send H--> open --send ES--> half-closed (local)).

NOT COLLECTED (no state transition): PRIORITY and WINDOW_UPDATE frames may be received in reserved (local), reserved (remote) and the half-closed states, and PRIORITY on closed streams, without any state transition (the per-state frame-type lists); CONTINUATION frames 'do not result in state transitions' (sec.5.1 note after Figure 2). No edges for them.

NOT COLLECTED (connection-level error exits): receiving any frame other than HEADERS or PRIORITY on an idle stream (and the per-state frame-type bans) is a CONNECTION error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR (sec.5.1), not a stream-state transition; the connection-error path is outside this case's scope.

NOT COLLECTED: closed-state late-frame handling (sec.5.1 'closed': minimal processing and discard; WINDOW_UPDATE or RST_STREAM may arrive for a short period after closing) causes no transition out of closed; Figure 2 draws no outgoing arrow from closed and none is transcribed.

KEPT, re-scoped: 'Receiving a PUSH_PROMISE frame also causes the promised stream to become "reserved (remote)", even when the PUSH_PROMISE frame is received on a closed stream.' (sec.5.1 'closed'). The re-reserved stream is the PROMISED (idle) stream, a different stream; its idle --recv PP--> reserved (remote) edge is already collected. No extra edge for the closed stream itself.
